question.text: What insurance must every registered vehicle in Nevada carry?

answer.text: All Nevada motorists must comply with mandatory insurance and financial responsibility laws, and every registered motor vehicle in the state must be covered by liability insurance.

teaching.text: Insurance is not optional in Nevada: every registered motor vehicle must carry liability coverage. Remember: liability insurance required.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: All Nevada motorists must comply with mandatory insurance and financial responsibility laws, and every registered motor vehicle in the state must be covered by liability insurance.

question.text: When do Nevada's minimum liability amounts apply?

answer.text: Nevada law sets minimum liability insurance amounts that apply whenever you drive or own a vehicle in the state.

teaching.text: The minimum liability amounts apply whenever you drive or own a vehicle in Nevada. Remember: drive or own, insure.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Nevada law sets minimum liability insurance amounts that apply whenever you drive or own a vehicle in the state.

question.text: How must you be able to show proof of insurance?

answer.text: Keep the insurer's Evidence of Insurance Card in the vehicle, or have it ready in electronic form to show on a mobile device.

teaching.text: Carry proof of insurance in the car, or keep the electronic version ready on your phone. Remember: card in car or phone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Keep the insurer's Evidence of Insurance Card in the vehicle, or have it ready in electronic form to show on a mobile device.

question.text: What are Nevada's minimum liability limits for injury or death?

answer.text: Nevada's minimum liability coverage is 25,000 dollars for injury or death of one person in a crash and 50,000 dollars for injury or death of two or more people in one crash.

teaching.text: The injury minimums are twenty-five thousand dollars for one person and fifty thousand dollars for two or more people in one crash. Remember: twenty-five, fifty for injuries.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Nevada's minimum liability coverage is 25,000 dollars for injury or death of one person in a crash and 50,000 dollars for injury or death of two or more people in one crash.

question.text: What is Nevada's minimum liability limit for property damage?

answer.text: Nevada's minimum liability coverage also includes 20,000 dollars for damage to or destruction of other people's property in any one crash.

teaching.text: Property damage coverage must be at least twenty thousand dollars per crash. Remember: twenty for property.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Nevada's minimum liability coverage also includes 20,000 dollars for damage to or destruction of other people's property in any one crash.

question.text: What does the NV LIVE program do?

answer.text: NV LIVE, the Nevada Liability Insurance Validation Electronically program, works with licensed insurers to flag registrations whose insurance has ended or lapsed.

teaching.text: NV LIVE links the DMV with licensed insurers so registrations with ended or lapsed coverage get flagged. Remember: NV LIVE flags lapses.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: NV LIVE, the Nevada Liability Insurance Validation Electronically program, works with licensed insurers to flag registrations whose insurance has ended or lapsed.

question.text: What do you pay if your registration is suspended for an insurance lapse?

answer.text: If a registration is suspended for an insurance lapse with no replacement coverage for that period, you pay a reinstatement fee plus fines starting at two hundred fifty dollars and reaching up to one thousand seven hundred fifty dollars for each vehicle on that policy.

teaching.text: A lapse with no replacement coverage brings a reinstatement fee plus fines from two hundred fifty to one thousand seven hundred fifty dollars per vehicle. Remember: fee plus rising fines.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If a registration is suspended for an insurance lapse with no replacement coverage for that period, you pay a reinstatement fee plus fines starting at two hundred fifty dollars and reaching up to one thousand seven hundred fifty dollars for each vehicle on that policy.

question.text: Do lapse fines apply once or for each vehicle on the policy?

answer.text: Lapse fines and the reinstatement fee apply to each registered vehicle that the lapsed policy covered.

teaching.text: The lapse fines and fee are charged for every registered vehicle the lapsed policy covered. Remember: fines per vehicle.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Lapse fines and the reinstatement fee apply to each registered vehicle that the lapsed policy covered.

question.text: What other penalties can follow an insurance lapse?

answer.text: Further penalties for an insurance lapse can include an SR-twenty-two requirement, a thirty-day driver license suspension, or both.

teaching.text: A lapse can also bring an SR-twenty-two requirement, a thirty-day license suspension, or both. Remember: SR-twenty-two, thirty-day suspension.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Further penalties for an insurance lapse can include an SR-twenty-two requirement, a thirty-day driver license suspension, or both.

question.text: How does a police-investigated crash reach the DMV?

answer.text: When law enforcement investigates a crash, the officer sends your insurance information and a description of the damage or injuries to the DMV.

teaching.text: When police investigate a crash, the officer sends your insurance details and a damage or injury description to the DMV. Remember: officer reports it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When law enforcement investigates a crash, the officer sends your insurance information and a description of the damage or injuries to the DMV.

question.text: When must you file an SR-one, and how soon?

answer.text: If police do not investigate a crash that causes seven hundred fifty dollars or more in damage or injures anyone, you must send a Report of Crash Form, the SR-one, to the DMV within ten days.

teaching.text: No police investigation, but injuries or seven hundred fifty dollars or more in damage? File the SR-one within ten days. Remember: no police? file in ten.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If police do not investigate a crash that causes seven hundred fifty dollars or more in damage or injures anyone, you must send a Report of Crash Form, the SR-one, to the DMV within ten days.

question.text: How does crash reporting differ when police investigate and when they do not?

answer.text: A police-investigated crash reaches the DMV through the officer's report, while a crash without police investigation that injures anyone or causes seven hundred fifty dollars or more in damage needs your own SR-one within ten days.

teaching.text: The officer reports investigated crashes; for uninvestigated crashes over the threshold, you file the SR-one yourself. Remember: officer or you report.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A police-investigated crash reaches the DMV through the officer's report, while a crash without police investigation that injures anyone or causes seven hundred fifty dollars or more in damage needs your own SR-one within ten days.

question.text: Who must complete the SR-one, and where do you get it?

answer.text: The SR-one must be completed by anyone who was the driver or the registered owner of a vehicle in the crash, and the form is available at DMV offices, the Nevada Highway Patrol, local police and the DMV website.

teaching.text: Every driver and registered owner in the crash completes an SR-one, available from the DMV, the Highway Patrol, local police or online. Remember: drivers and owners file.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The SR-one must be completed by anyone who was the driver or the registered owner of a vehicle in the crash, and the form is available at DMV offices, the Nevada Highway Patrol, local police and the DMV website.

question.text: What does the DMV Financial Responsibility Section decide after a crash?

answer.text: After a crash, the DMV Financial Responsibility Section decides who was at fault, whether every vehicle and driver was insured, and the total liability.

teaching.text: The DMV's Financial Responsibility Section decides fault, whether everyone was insured, and the total liability. Remember: fault, insurance, liability.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After a crash, the DMV Financial Responsibility Section decides who was at fault, whether every vehicle and driver was insured, and the total liability.

question.text: What can happen to an at-fault driver without liability insurance?

answer.text: An at-fault driver without liability insurance may have the license or registration suspended, must post a deposit with the DMV to cover crash costs, or must arrange payment with the other parties.

teaching.text: Uninsured and at fault means a possible suspension, a deposit with the DMV, or an arranged payment to the other parties. Remember: suspension, deposit or payment.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An at-fault driver without liability insurance may have the license or registration suspended, must post a deposit with the DMV to cover crash costs, or must arrange payment with the other parties.

question.text: What can happen if you fail to report a crash to the DMV?

answer.text: Failing to report a crash to the DMV can lead to suspension of your driver license, your vehicle registration, or both.

teaching.text: Not reporting a crash can cost you your license, your registration, or both. Remember: unreported crash, suspension.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Failing to report a crash to the DMV can lead to suspension of your driver license, your vehicle registration, or both.

question.text: What is an SR-twenty-two?

answer.text: An SR-twenty-two is liability insurance on a driver license that lets the DMV monitor the insurance of a suspended or revoked driver through reports from the insurer, and it may be required for reinstatement.

teaching.text: An SR-twenty-two is insurance on your license that the DMV monitors through your insurer during reinstatement. Remember: monitored proof of insurance.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An SR-twenty-two is liability insurance on a driver license that lets the DMV monitor the insurance of a suspended or revoked driver through reports from the insurer, and it may be required for reinstatement.

question.text: When does SR-twenty-two coverage start, and when should you buy it?

answer.text: SR-twenty-two coverage starts when you actually reinstate, you file the form only once, and you should not buy it until every other reinstatement requirement is met.

teaching.text: SR-twenty-two coverage begins when you reinstate, is filed once, and should be bought only after every other requirement is met. Remember: buy it last.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: SR-twenty-two coverage starts when you actually reinstate, you file the form only once, and you should not buy it until every other reinstatement requirement is met.

question.text: How do the SR-one and SR-twenty-two differ?

answer.text: The SR-one is a crash report you file, while the SR-twenty-two is proof-of-insurance coverage that the DMV monitors when reinstating a suspended or revoked driver.

teaching.text: The SR-one reports a crash; the SR-twenty-two proves ongoing insurance for reinstatement. Remember: report versus coverage.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The SR-one is a crash report you file, while the SR-twenty-two is proof-of-insurance coverage that the DMV monitors when reinstating a suspended or revoked driver.

question.text: What decides the cost of SR-twenty-two coverage?

answer.text: The price of SR-twenty-two coverage depends on how the insurance company structures it.

teaching.text: How much an SR-twenty-two costs depends on how the insurance company structures it. Remember: insurer sets the price.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The price of SR-twenty-two coverage depends on how the insurance company structures it.

question.text: What are the first duties at a crash scene?

answer.text: At a crash, stop, get medical help for anyone injured, warn traffic and notify law enforcement.

teaching.text: At any crash: stop, get medical help for the injured, warn traffic, and notify law enforcement. Remember: stop, help, warn, notify.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a crash, stop, get medical help for anyone injured, warn traffic and notify law enforcement.

question.text: What should you do after a fender bender with no injuries?

answer.text: In a fender bender with only property damage and no injuries, move the vehicle if it can be moved safely to a spot that does not block traffic, then return to the scene.

teaching.text: In a no-injury fender bender with drivable cars, move out of traffic if safe, then return to the scene. Remember: move aside, come back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a fender bender with only property damage and no injuries, move the vehicle if it can be moved safely to a spot that does not block traffic, then return to the scene.

question.text: How do the first steps differ for an injury crash and a fender bender?

answer.text: If a crash involves injuries, the first duties are to stop, get medical help and warn traffic; the move-it-aside rule covers a fender bender with property damage only and a vehicle that can be moved safely.

teaching.text: With injuries, helping people and warning traffic come first; moving aside is for property-only crashes. Remember: injuries first, then move.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If a crash involves injuries, the first duties are to stop, get medical help and warn traffic; the move-it-aside rule covers a fender bender with property damage only and a vehicle that can be moved safely.

question.text: What information must you exchange with other drivers after a crash?

answer.text: Exchange your name, address, driver license number, registration and insurance information with every other driver involved.

teaching.text: Trade your name, address, license number, registration and insurance information with every other driver. Remember: swap the five details.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Exchange your name, address, driver license number, registration and insurance information with every other driver involved.

question.text: What must you do after hitting an unattended vehicle or property?

answer.text: If you hit an unattended vehicle or other property, give the owner your name, address, license number, registration and insurance details, in person or in a note left behind.

teaching.text: Hit an unattended car or property? Give the owner your details, face to face or in a note. Remember: leave your details.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you hit an unattended vehicle or other property, give the owner your name, address, license number, registration and insurance details, in person or in a note left behind.

question.text: Why can a Nevada driver license be suspended, revoked or canceled?

answer.text: A Nevada driver license is a privilege, and it can be suspended, revoked or canceled if you stop driving safely and obeying the rules.

teaching.text: Your license is a privilege that unsafe driving or breaking the rules can cost you. Remember: license is a privilege.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Nevada driver license is a privilege, and it can be suspended, revoked or canceled if you stop driving safely and obeying the rules.

question.text: What goes on your Nevada driving record?

answer.text: Crashes and traffic convictions go on your driving record, including violations committed in other states.

teaching.text: Crashes and convictions, including those from other states, all go on your Nevada record. Remember: out-of-state tickets count.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Crashes and traffic convictions go on your driving record, including violations committed in other states.

question.text: How long do most violations and DUI convictions stay reportable?

answer.text: Most violations can be reported to your insurer for three years, while convictions related to driving under the influence stay on the record for seven years.

teaching.text: Most violations stay reportable to insurers for three years, and DUI convictions stay for seven. Remember: three years, DUI seven.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Most violations can be reported to your insurer for three years, while convictions related to driving under the influence stay on the record for seven years.

question.text: Which stays longer on your record, most violations or a DUI conviction?

answer.text: Most violations stay reportable to insurers for three years, while DUI-related convictions stay on the record for seven years.

teaching.text: DUI convictions outlast ordinary violations on your record: seven years against three. Remember: DUI stays longer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Most violations stay reportable to insurers for three years, while DUI-related convictions stay on the record for seven years.

question.text: When are demerit points added, and over what period are they counted?

answer.text: Every traffic violation carries demerit points, added once a court sends the DMV notice of a conviction or civil infraction, and points are counted over a twelve-month period.

teaching.text: Points are added when a court notifies the DMV of a conviction, and they are counted over twelve months. Remember: points over twelve months.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every traffic violation carries demerit points, added once a court sends the DMV notice of a conviction or civil infraction, and points are counted over a twelve-month period.

question.text: How many demerit points in twelve months lead to suspension?

answer.text: Receiving twelve or more demerit points in any twelve-month period means your license will be suspended.

teaching.text: Twelve or more points in any twelve-month period means a license suspension. Remember: twelve in twelve suspends.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Receiving twelve or more demerit points in any twelve-month period means your license will be suspended.

question.text: How can traffic school help with demerit points?

answer.text: With three to eleven points, completing a DMV-approved traffic safety course removes up to three points, but only once in any twelve-month period, and the conviction itself stays in your driving history.

teaching.text: With three to eleven points, a DMV-approved course can remove up to three points once in twelve months, but the conviction stays. Remember: school takes three, once.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: With three to eleven points, completing a DMV-approved traffic safety course removes up to three points, but only once in any twelve-month period, and the conviction itself stays in your driving history.

question.text: When are traffic school points actually removed?

answer.text: Points from traffic school are removed only when the school reports your completion for credit, and the DMV will notify you if unsafe driving puts your license status in jeopardy.

teaching.text: Traffic school points come off only once the school reports your completion, and the DMV warns you when your license is in jeopardy. Remember: removed when reported.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Points from traffic school are removed only when the school reports your completion for credit, and the DMV will notify you if unsafe driving puts your license status in jeopardy.

question.text: What happens after a conviction for a major offense such as DUI?

answer.text: A conviction for a major offense such as DUI or causing substantial bodily harm revokes the license; these offenses carry no demerit points.

teaching.text: Major offenses like DUI or causing substantial bodily harm bring revocation, not demerit points. Remember: major offense revokes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A conviction for a major offense such as DUI or causing substantial bodily harm revokes the license; these offenses carry no demerit points.

question.text: How does points-based suspension differ from revocation?

answer.text: Points-based suspension comes from reaching twelve points within twelve months, while revocation follows a single major conviction such as DUI that carries no points at all.

teaching.text: Points lead to suspension at twelve in twelve months; one major conviction like DUI leads to revocation. Remember: points suspend, DUI revokes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Points-based suspension comes from reaching twelve points within twelve months, while revocation follows a single major conviction such as DUI that carries no points at all.

question.text: How many points do reckless driving, careless driving and failing to aid carry?

answer.text: Demerit points: reckless driving is eight points, and careless driving or failing to give information or render aid at a crash scene is six points.

teaching.text: Reckless driving costs eight points; careless driving and failing to give information or aid at a crash cost six. Remember: reckless eight, careless six.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Demerit points: reckless driving is eight points, and careless driving or failing to give information or render aid at a crash scene is six points.

question.text: Which carries more points, reckless or careless driving?

answer.text: Reckless driving carries eight demerit points while careless driving carries six.

teaching.text: Reckless driving is eight points and careless driving is six, so the names sound alike but the points differ. Remember: reckless outweighs careless.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Reckless driving carries eight demerit points while careless driving carries six.

question.text: Which common violations carry four points each?

answer.text: Demerit points: following too closely, failing to yield the right-of-way, failing to yield to a pedestrian, and disobeying a traffic signal or stop sign are four points each.

teaching.text: Following too closely, failing to yield to vehicles or pedestrians, and running a signal or stop sign are four points each. Remember: four for yield failures.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Demerit points: following too closely, failing to yield the right-of-way, failing to yield to a pedestrian, and disobeying a traffic signal or stop sign are four points each.

question.text: Which violations carry two points each?

answer.text: Demerit points: impeding traffic or driving too slowly, failing to dim headlights, and a prima facie speed violation or driving too fast for conditions are two points each.

teaching.text: Driving too slowly, failing to dim headlights, and driving too fast for conditions are two points each. Remember: two for slow or dim.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Demerit points: impeding traffic or driving too slowly, failing to dim headlights, and a prima facie speed violation or driving too fast for conditions are two points each.

question.text: How do the points for driving too fast for conditions compare with speeding?

answer.text: A prima facie speed violation or driving too fast for conditions costs two points, the same as speeding eleven to twenty miles per hour over the limit.

teaching.text: Driving too fast for conditions costs two points, the same as speeding eleven to twenty miles per hour over. Remember: conditions equal mid speeding.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A prima facie speed violation or driving too fast for conditions costs two points, the same as speeding eleven to twenty miles per hour over the limit.

question.text: How do speeding points rise with speed over the limit?

answer.text: Speeding points rise with speed over the limit: one to ten miles per hour over is one point, eleven to twenty is two points, twenty-one to thirty is three points, thirty-one to forty is four points, and forty-one miles per hour or more is five points.

teaching.text: Speeding points climb by bands: one point for one to ten over, up to five points for forty-one or more over. Remember: faster over, more points.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Speeding points rise with speed over the limit: one to ten miles per hour over is one point, eleven to twenty is two points, twenty-one to thirty is three points, thirty-one to forty is four points, and forty-one miles per hour or more is five points.

question.text: Is the handbook's point list complete, and do commercial drivers face more?

answer.text: The point list is only partial, and holders of a commercial driver license may face extra penalties and points for some violations.

teaching.text: The point list in the handbook is only partial, and commercial license holders may face extra points. Remember: partial list, CDL more.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The point list is only partial, and holders of a commercial driver license may face extra penalties and points for some violations.

question.text: What can a free online DMV account show you?

answer.text: A free online account through the DMV website shows license status and expiration, a driver history printout, and full lists of demerit points, violation codes and court details.

teaching.text: A free online DMV account shows your license status, a driver history printout, and full point and violation lists. Remember: online record, free.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A free online account through the DMV website shows license status and expiration, a driver history printout, and full lists of demerit points, violation codes and court details.

question.text: What license misuse is illegal in Nevada?

answer.text: It is illegal to give false information on a Nevada license application, to alter your license, to lend it to anyone, or to use another person's license.

teaching.text: Never give false application details, alter your license, lend it, or use someone else's. Remember: no lending, no altering.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: It is illegal to give false information on a Nevada license application, to alter your license, to lend it to anyone, or to use another person's license.
